rows.evidence: No verified free recording found: LibriVox has no reading of this 1519 sermon; the similar-sounding 'How to Meditate upon and Apply the Death and Sacrifice of Christ' in Select Works Vol 1 turned out to be a Galatians 1:4 extract; and Pastor Wolfmueller's podcast episode 'Introduction to the Meditation on the Passion of Christ' does not name this sermon.

Searches of the LibriVox catalogue and API, Internet Archive audio and the web turned up text editions only (Gutenberg, Works of Martin Luther Vol. II), with no human-read recording of this 1519 sermon.

The only free readings of Luther on Luke 2 found are Pastor Wolfmueller's House Postil Christmas sermons, which are not this 1521 Church Postil sermon, and a LibriVox track of the Bible text 'Lukas 2, Vers 1-14', which is not a sermon.
Only text versions (CTSFW PDF, godrules.net) and discussion podcasts (Issues, Etc., 1517) turned up; no LibriVox, Internet Archive or ministry reading of the eight Invocavit sermons was found.

The LibriVox page for Epistle Sermons, Volume 2 (Lenker translation) lists section 4, 'Third Sunday After Epiphany.—Christian Revenge. Romans 12, 16-21' (read by Brize C, 10:34), with play and MP3 download links.

The LibriVox page for Epistle Sermons, Volume 2 lists section 5, 'Fourth Sunday After Epiphany.—Christian Love and the Command to Love. Romans 13, 8-10' (read by Laurel Monroe, 54:10), with play and MP3 download links.

The LibriVox page for Epistle Sermons, Volume 2 lists section 6, 'Fifth Sunday After Epiphany.—The Glorious Adornment of Christians. Colossians 3, 12-17' (read by Kazbek, 50:35), with play and MP3 download links.

The LibriVox page for Epistle Sermons, Volume 2 lists section 9, 'Sunday Before Lent.—Paul's Praise of Christian Love. 1 Corinthians 13' (read by Charles Zwick Jr., 40:49), with play and MP3 download links.
The English text is the in-copyright Luther's Works vol. 51 translation, and no free rights-holder or ministry recording of this 1530 Coburg sermon turned up (LCMS and 1517 have articles only).
Only text editions (godrules.net, German History Intersections, archive.org scans) turned up; no LibriVox, Internet Archive or ministry audio of this 1530 sermon was found.
LibriVox's 'The Sermon on the Mount - Commentary' is Chrysostom's homilies, not Luther's; Hay's translation of Luther exists only as text (archive.org, Monergism), with no free human reading found.

LibriVox has recorded only Epistle Sermons Volume 2 (Epiphany to Pentecost), not Volume 3 (Trinity to Advent), which holds this sermon; Wolfmueller's Trinity 2 episode is the gospel sermon on Luke 14, not this epistle sermon on 1 John 3.

The online texts found (Immanuel Lutheran, SermonCentral) reproduce the in-copyright Luther's Works vol. 51 translation as text only, and no free authorised recording of this last Eisleben sermon was found.
